content: I've been implementing sound and complete Hilbert systems for the snce and untl operators, working backwards from the bimodal logic developed for reasoning about non-deterministic dynamical systems with both tense and modal operators. I have finished 2/4 of the completeness results for the base logic and its dense extension, with the continuous and discrete extensions underway. Loads of clean up to do also, so beware, but here is what I have so far: https://github.com/benbrastmckie/cslib/tree/main/Cslib/Logics/Temporal
Just submitted a first Temporal/ PR stacked on this Propositional/ PR.

Looking at your MCS and Deduction Theorem proofs for temporal logic, I think we can abstract away from proving this stuff repeatedly by using classes.

For instance, all you need is ⊢ φ → ψ → φ, ⊢ (φ → ψ → χ) → (φ → ψ) → φ → χ, and ⊢ φ → ψ ⟹ ⊢ φ ⟹ ⊢ ψ and you can prove the deduction theorem (here's my formalization in Isabelle).

Similarly, we could show, given those same axioms, that if Γ ⊬ ϕ then Γ can be extended to an MCS Ω where Ω ⊬ ϕ, and prove common results like ϕ ∈ Ω ⇔ Ω ⊢ ϕ and so on.

Benjamin Brast-McKie said:

Just submitted a first Temporal/ PR stacked on this Propositional/ PR.

Would it maybe make sense to formalize LTL? This would open up the exploration of Büchi automata. The translation of LTL formulae to Büchi automata has been formally verified before by Schimpf et al., but the code is no longer available, sadly.
Büchi automata and the closure of omega-regular languages under boolean operations are already in cslib.

I don't have any metalogical results for LTL, but definitely makes sense to include. I was thinking something along these lines:

    PropositionalConnectives
        (HasBot + HasImp)
                    |
          FutureTemporalConnectives
            (+ HasUntil)
           /                 \
LTLConnectives      TemporalConnectives
 (+ HasNext)               (+ HasSince)

I have implemented Burgess/Xu's soundness and completeness for TemporalConnectives over all linear orders, where the logic may be strengthened for discrete linear orders, or alternatively to dense linear orders, as well as to complete linear orders. I would be excited to contribute these results. I'm still moving over the results for the discrete and continuous extensions.

In Connectives.lean, BimodalConnectives extends ModalConnectives (which includes HasBox) and adds HasUntil and HasSince directly as atomic mixins, avoiding a typeclass diamond through PropositionalConnectives. The resulting logic is proved sound and complete over non-deterministic dynamical systems. I was thinking this should belong in Bimodal/ rather than Temporal/ since it combines operators from both Temporal/ and Modal/. I have only moved dense completeness so far, and am still cleaning things up.

Following up on the LTL and Büchi-automata question, I implemented Cslib/Logics/LTL which builds on the existing ω-automata library. Here is an inventory of what is established so far.

On the syntax side, LTL formulas are built from {atom, bot, imp, next, untl} in Formula. The next-step operator next (◯) is kept as a primitive constructor rather than derived as ⊥ U φ (using the Pnueli for order of the arguments untl guard event), since that encoding only holds on discrete non-ending sequences.

On the semantic side, truth over ω-sequences is Satisfies, using the reflexive (non-strict) until ∃ j ≥ i, with Valid and Satisfiable, and the derived ◇/□ operators characterized by someFuture_iff and allFuture_iff. There is also an execution-based semantics over a labelled transition system, SatisfiesExec, proved to agree with the sequence semantics via satisfiesExec_iff_satisfies_setWord.

The headline result is ω-regularity. The ω-language of a formula is Formula.omegaLanguage, and Formula.isRegular proves that every LTL formula over a finite atom set defines an ω-regular language. The untl case rests on the LTL-to-Büchi translation that came up above: Formula.gnba_language_eq (Baier-Katoen Theorem 5.39) shows the generalized Büchi (GNBA) tableau construction for φ accepts exactly φ's ω-language, built on the Büchi automata already in the library.

That machinery then yields model checking: ltlModelChecking (Baier-Katoen Theorem 5.47) gives the standard reduction for a finite-state LTS — every ω-execution from every initial state satisfies φ if and only if the product of the LTS with the GNBA for ¬φ has no reachable accepting cycle. The bridge to the language formulation is satisfiesExec_iff_mem_omegaLanguage.

Finally, Formula.toTemporal embeds LTL into the Temporal BX syntax, bridging the convention swap by mapping untl guard event to the reflexive reflexiveUntl and next φ to the strict untl ⊥ φ, which forces the witness to be the immediate successor on ℕ. For uniformity, I aim to transition away from the Burgess conventions for untl and snce, but haven't done so yet. Would be very curious if anyone has thoughts or suggestions.

Also, here is an inventory of what is established in Cslib/Logics/Temporal so far.

On the syntax and proof-theory side, formulas are built from {atom, bot, imp, untl, snce} in Formula. The Burgess-Xu (BX) Hilbert system is the Axiom schema (4 propositional plus 22 temporal constructors), with the strengthenings for each frame class indexed by FrameClass. Derivability is given by Derivable, with the theorem-level abbreviations ThDerivable and the frame-parametric ThDerivableFc.

On the semantic side, models are TemporalModel over a linear-order time domain, truth is Satisfies, and the validity hierarchy (Valid, ValidSerial, ValidDense, ValidDiscrete) is set up in Validity.lean.

The metalogical machinery is also complete: the deductionTheorem by well-founded recursion on derivation height, the Lindenbaum extension temporal_lindenbaum (every consistent set extends to an MCS) together with the standard MCS closure properties, and the chronicle chronicle_truth_lemma connecting satisfaction in the chronicle countermodel to MCS membership.

The two headline metalogical results that are finished are for the base logic over serial linear orders and for its dense extension. For the base logic: soundness (with the derivable-formula corollary soundness_thderivable) and completeness, which proves that validity over all serial linear orders implies BX-derivability via the chronicle limit countermodel built on a subtype of ℚ. For the dense extension: soundness_dense and completeness_dense.

There is also a conservativity result: BX is a conservative extension of classical propositional logic, temporal_conservative_extension, via the structural embedding in FromPropositional.lean.

That accounts for 2 of the 4 completeness results (base and dense). The discrete and continuous/complete extensions are still being moved over and cleaned up, along with the tableau development in Temporal/Tableau.

As I've mentioned before, rather than proving the deduction theorem repeatedly, I think you can just do it once using an axiom class which reflects the Hilbert system for IPL⟨→,⊤⟩. Then all of the structural logics that extend IPL⟨→,⊤⟩ will have it; moreover, you can make another axiom class for the deduction theorem and modus ponens, and show that it instances the IPL⟨→,⊤⟩ class, since IPL⟨→,⊤⟩ is the weakest logic that proves the deduction theorem.

Benjamin Brast-McKie said:

The next-step operator next (◯) is kept as a primitive constructor rather than derived as φ U ⊥, since that encoding only holds on discrete non-ending sequences. LTL uses the standard (Pnueli) convention untl guard event and formulas are Encodable whenever the atoms are.

I don't understand the above sentence. φ U ⊥ is equivalent to ⊥. I don't think "next" can be expressed using "until", or vice versa.
@Benjamin Brast-McKie I hope you did not write the above using AI.

Sorry that was my mistake getting mixed up between Burgess's convention which flips the arguments. I changed it above to stay consistent with Pnueli convention, and will do so throughout.

I also realize I didn't provide adequate context for that comment to make sense. Given a strict semantics where φ U ψ is true at t iff there is an s > t with ψ true at s and φ true at r for all r in the open interval (t, s), setting the guard to ⊥ forces the interval (t, s) to be empty, and so Xφ means φ is true at the immediate successor of t. This coincides with the standard LTL next operator on discrete frames, where every time has an immediate successor; on dense frames it is never satisfiable, because no such successor exists, and so is equivalent to ⊥.

In the usual computer science convention, ⊥ U φ is equivalent to φ; see:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_temporal_logic#Semantics

I maintained those conventions for LTL. The broader temporal logic requires greater expressive power by assuming the strict semantics in order to establish completeness for the base tense logic BX and its various discrete, dense, and continuous extensions. For instance, the density axioms are trivially satisfied without assuming a strict semantics. To avoid conflating these different notions, it might make sense to use U' and S' in contrast to U and S. I can revise the notation and include docstrings to help clarify.

Do you have a reference for the conventions you are using? The Wikipedia article I pointed to uses the standard computer science convention, in which neither "next" nor "until" can be expressed in terms of the other.
